drafted_from: tools/grade-and-repair-speech-audio/tool-rows.json (tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio), do-work/grade_and_repair_speech.py, read-data/grade_rules.py and spans.py, test/grade-and-repair-speech-audio.test.mjs and its fixture (build_fixture.py, settings-for-synthetic-speech.json)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Grade the speech in the three spans of /Work/demo/spans.json against my settings in /Work/settings.json and clean up the ones that sound poor, writing to /Work/demo/out." It runs tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio on your computer and tells you how many spans were good, remastered or need a clone.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a spans file and settings file on your computer and writes grades.json and audio files into a folder you name.
instructions: 1. Install it as the row says (ffmpeg, numpy, scipy, soundfile, mlx-whisper; DeepFilterNet in its own venv is optional) and write your settings file with every key in read-data/settings-keys.json; take the values from your own records, never from the tool.
2. Write a spans file: {"spans":[{"clip","source","from","to","text","words":[{"text","start","end"}]}]}. Words with times give a better noise reading and are needed to clone later.

3. Say "Grade the speech in my spans file". Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool:"tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio"} and runs its run command with your spans file, a new output folder and your settings (use `grade` instead of `all` to measure and grade without remastering).

4. Read the last JSON line ({result:{grades,counts:{good,remaster,clone}}}) and grades.json: for each span that was not good, the reasons. Spans marked clone go to tool:clone-speech-that-repair-could-not-fix.

worked_examples.title: Three synthetic recordings graded: one kept as it is, two sent to remaster
worked_examples.ask: Grade the speech in my three spans against my settings and tell me which sound poor.
worked_examples.given: From tools/grade-and-repair-speech-audio/test/grade-and-repair-speech-audio.test.mjs, run here for real with its `grade` stage (the stage `all` adds the remaster and needs whisper and DeepFilterNet weights): a spans file /Work/demo/spans.json with three spans of three synthetic recordings (clean.wav, noisy.wav with a 60 Hz hum and loud floor, clipped.wav driven into clipping), each from 0.4 to 5.0 s with its five word times, and one repeat of the first and test/settings-for-synthetic-speech.json. The AI first reads the row with this tools:list call, then runs: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/grade-and-repair-speech-audio/do-work/grade_and_repair_speech.py grade --spans /Work/demo/spans.json --settings /Work/settings.json --out /Work/demo/out. The answer's paths are shown for the output folder /Work/demo/out (the run was made in a temporary folder; the counts are as printed).
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints clean_0.40_5.00 good, noisy_0.40_5.00 remaster, clipped_0.40_5.00 remaster (the repeated cut is graded once), then {"result": {"grades": "/Work/demo/out/grades.json", "counts": {"good": 1, "remaster": 2, "clone": 0}}}. grades.json gives clean treatment as-is with audio audio/clean_0.40_5.00.wav (0.2 s handle either side, snr 66.6 dB); noisy reasons: "noise: snr 18.6 dB < 30 (floor -32.3 dBFS)", "hum: 150 Hz stands 23.3 dB above its neighbours", "wind/rumble: 69% of the noise below 120 Hz"; clipped reasons: "clipping: 0.2024 of samples at full scale, true peak 0.21 dB" and "loudness: -5.32 LUFS outside -26..-10".
